candidates.name: Corneal amyloidosis
support_spans: 4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma
Ring characteristics: Complete rings, outermost ring ~4mm from limbus
candidates.why: The presence of ring-shaped opacities in the posterior corneal stroma is consistent with Corneal amyloidosis.

candidates.name: Posterior crocodile shagreen
support_spans: Peripheral cornea: posterior crocodile shagreen
candidates.why: The presence of posterior crocodile shagreen is a specific finding that can be associated with certain corneal conditions.

candidates.name: Fuchs endothelial dystrophy
support_spans: Mild nuclear sclerosis of crystalline lens in both eyes
Normal corneal sensations bilaterally
candidates.why: The combination of corneal findings and mild nuclear sclerosis may suggest a disease mechanism related to Fuchs endothelial dystrophy.

candidates.name: Lattice corneal dystrophy
support_spans: 4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in posterior corneal stroma
candidates.why: The presence of ring-shaped opacities is consistent with Lattice corneal dystrophy, which is caused by mutations in the TGFBI gene.

candidates.name: Granular corneal dystrophy
support_spans: Laser scanning in vivo confocal microscopy (HRT II with RCM): Revealed long bandlike structures with thin streaks of white lines interspersed
candidates.why: The findings on confocal microscopy are consistent with Granular corneal dystrophy, which can be confirmed with this modality.

candidates.name: Macular corneal dystrophy
support_spans: Slit-lamp examination images: Shows 4 corneal ring opacities in both eyes, alternatively distinct with outermost and third rings more sharply demarcated
candidates.why: The presence of corneal ring opacities on slit-lamp examination can be diagnostic for Macular corneal dystrophy.
